caution: This watch follows public evidence of accountability, implementation and reporting. An absence of public evidence is not evidence that no action or outcome occurred.

change_detection.review_rule: Deterministic changes create a review item; they do not publish a new conclusion or status automatically.

chains.title: In Plain Sight implementation and reporting
chains.originating_concern: The 2020 independent review documented widespread Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination in B.C. health care.
chains.key_finding: The review issued 24 recommendations for systemic change.
chains.recommendation_or_commitment: The Province and health-sector partners committed to act on the recommendations.
chains.implementation_action_claimed: Public reporting describes legal, regulatory, governance and patient-feedback actions.
chains.implementation_evidence: The 24-month report and later Action 3.07 reporting document activity, while Action 3.07 says comprehensive reporting capacity is limited.
chains.unresolved_gap: No current recommendation-by-recommendation public status ledger was located for all 24 recommendations.
chains.contradictions_or_limitations: Activity, policy adoption and program creation are not equivalent to provincewide operation or measured outcomes.
chains.best_next_document: A current 24-row status ledger naming each responsible organization, implementation evidence and outcome measure.
chains.evidence_quality: Original independent review plus official implementation reports; outcome coverage remains incomplete.

sources.title: In Plain Sight Task Team 24-Month Report

chains.title: First Nations Health Ombudsperson Office inaugural reporting
chains.originating_concern: First Nations leaders created a culturally grounded route for health-care complaints, advocacy, resolution and investigation.
chains.key_finding: The inaugural report records 391 complaints from July 2023 to March 2025 and identifies four systemic recommendation themes.
chains.recommendation_or_commitment: Saskatchewan’s Ministry of Health and Saskatchewan Health Authority stated they were reviewing the report and recommendations.
chains.implementation_action_claimed: FNHO reports case-level resolution work; government reported review of its recommendations.
chains.implementation_evidence: The inaugural report documents case-specific activity, and Hansard records the Ministry/SHA review statement.
chains.unresolved_gap: No later recommendation-level Ministry or SHA implementation response was located.
chains.contradictions_or_limitations: Closed or resolved complaints and continued funding do not establish systemwide implementation.
chains.best_next_document: A Ministry/SHA response that maps each FNHO recommendation to an owner, action and evidence of progress.
chains.evidence_quality: First Nations-governed primary reporting plus a legislative response statement; later implementation reporting is limited.

chains.title: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate
chains.originating_concern: An Indigenous advisory panel called for a more accountable response to racism and patient concerns.
chains.key_finding: The advocate has a bounded Health Charter review and advisory role, but no general disciplinary power.
chains.recommendation_or_commitment: Alberta created the role within the Office of Alberta Health Advocates.
responsible_organizations: health authorities and organizations receiving recommendations
chains.implementation_action_claimed: The office provides complaint support, navigation, bounded review and system advice.
chains.implementation_evidence: The service page and 2026–29 business plan document operation; the plan reports 321 correspondence items in 2025.
chains.unresolved_gap: A public ledger of cases, recommendations, responses and outcomes was not located.
chains.contradictions_or_limitations: Correspondence volume is not a count of complaints, investigations, resolutions or outcomes.
chains.best_next_document: An annual public report with aggregate caseload, recommendation, response-time and outcome measures.
chains.evidence_quality: Official mandate and business-plan sources support operation and a narrow correspondence metric; role-specific outcomes remain unreported.

chains.title: Saskatoon coerced-sterilization review and response
chains.originating_concern: A commissioned external review documented reported experiences of seven Indigenous women concerning pressure or coercion around tubal ligation.
chains.key_finding: The review issued ten Calls to Action and treated the accounts as a cohort/systemic concern.
chains.recommendation_or_commitment: Saskatoon Health Region apologized; SHA links the Indigenous Birth Support Worker Program to the review.
responsible_organizations: governments responsible for distinct legal and policy actions
accountable_actors: Court of King’s Bench for Saskatchewan for procedural litigation matters
chains.implementation_action_claimed: SHA states the Birth Support Worker Program was created in response and continues at Jim Pattison Children’s Hospital.
chains.implementation_evidence: SHA evaluation and current service-page material support an operating program and local evaluation.
chains.unresolved_gap: Current status for most Calls to Action and a provincewide consent-policy audit were not located.
chains.contradictions_or_limitations: The 2025 class-certification decision was procedural and did not decide the truth of individual reported experiences.
chains.best_next_document: An SHA ten-Call implementation table with evidence, scope and outcome measures.
chains.evidence_quality: Commissioned external review plus current health-system program evidence and a direct procedural legal source.

chains.title: Alberta Indigenous Primary Health Care Advisory Panel
chains.originating_concern: Alberta convened an Indigenous advisory panel to address culturally safe, Indigenous-led and accountable primary health care.
chains.key_finding: The panel made 22 recommendations and government published a separate implementation plan.
chains.recommendation_or_commitment: The Way Forward and related government pages describe implementation, funding and oversight mechanisms.
accountable_actors: Indigenous Primary Health Care Advisory Panel context
chains.implementation_action_claimed: Navigator grants, an innovation fund, an Indigenous Health Division and a patient-safety advocate are publicly documented.
chains.implementation_evidence: Official plan, program and funding pages document named mechanisms and some completed/underway work.
chains.unresolved_gap: A current 22-recommendation status ledger and outcome evidence for funded mechanisms were not located.
chains.contradictions_or_limitations: Program creation and listed actions are not evidence of provincewide service reach, sustained operation or effectiveness.
chains.best_next_document: A current public 22-recommendation implementation and outcome ledger, including geographic service coverage.
chains.evidence_quality: Original advisory report and official implementation sources establish named actions; recommendation-level outcomes are incomplete.

chains.title: Maskwacis youth fatality inquiry and recommendation responses
chains.originating_concern: A public fatality inquiry examined the deaths by suicide of four First Nations young people from the four Nations of Maskwacis between 2017 and 2020.
chains.key_finding: The inquiry described barriers spanning child and family services, mental-health supports, information sharing, funding and coordination, and issued 44 recommendations according to the public report and Indigenous reporting.
chains.recommendation_or_commitment: The public response tracker records 62 responder rows covering 40 distinct numbered recommendations, including healthcare recommendations to Alberta Health Services and provincial and federal organizations.
responsible_organizations: Delegated First Nations Agencies and local service partners named by the inquiry
chains.implementation_action_claimed: The tracker records categories including accepted, accepted in principle, not accepted, other, waiting for response and no response recorded for named responder rows.
chains.implementation_evidence: The tracker establishes that responses were requested and records response categories. It does not provide a complete implementation or outcome ledger, and five healthcare responder rows were still marked waiting for response when reviewed.
chains.unresolved_gap: Recommendation-level claimed actions, implementation evidence, outcomes and independent verification are not consistently available in the structured tracker.
chains.contradictions_or_limitations: Forty numbered recommendations appear in the current response tracker while the inquiry/reporting describes 44. Responder labels are not evidence that a recommendation was implemented.
chains.best_next_document: Full response letters and a recommendation-by-recommendation implementation and outcome update, especially for AHS recommendations 12, 13, 28, 29 and 35.
chains.evidence_quality: Public fatality-inquiry report, structured official response tracker and Indigenous-media reporting; implementation evidence remains limited.

chains.title: Solonas inquest Indigenous-support recommendation
chains.originating_concern: The inquest into Nadine Marcy Solonas’s death reviewed police custody, mistrust of first responders, paramedic assessment, emergency care and transfer after a serious assault.
chains.key_finding: The jury recommended a 24-hour, on-call Indigenous support position for Indigenous people in RCMP custody who refuse treatment or mistrust first responders.
chains.recommendation_or_commitment: The recommendation was directed to the Deputy Commissioner of RCMP E Division and specified a non-uniformed civilian role supporting a culturally safe environment.
responsible_organizations: Royal Canadian Mounted Police, E Division
chains.implementation_action_claimed: No recommendation-specific public action statement was located in the sources reviewed.
chains.implementation_evidence: No public evidence confirming creation or evaluation of the recommended position was located.
chains.unresolved_gap: Whether the RCMP responded to or implemented the recommendation remains unclear from public sources.
chains.contradictions_or_limitations: The inquest was fact-finding, not fault-finding. The verdict records that the Independent Investigations Office found no police action or inaction contributed to the death, and the jury did not make a finding of racism.
chains.best_next_document: A recommendation-specific RCMP response or later public evaluation of an on-call Indigenous support role in B.C. custody settings.
chains.evidence_quality: Official jury verdict and Indigenous-media corroboration; recommendation follow-up was not located.
